findings.title: P1: authenticated outsiders can read private league details and coach emails
findings.acceptance: Private league DTOs and cached reads reject outsiders and exclude account emails.
findings.verifiedBy: Gibs security/QA agent; parent independently reran real PostgreSQL HTTP regression on 2026-09-14

findings.title: P1 conditional security blocker: enabling play-by-play enables arbitrary external result submission
findings.acceptance: PBP uses authorized server sessions; fabricated, stale, foreign and reported-mode finalizations fail with no mutations.
findings.verifiedBy: Containment only: Gibs security/QA agent and parent HTTP rerun; authoritative sessions still due W08

findings.title: P1: invalid box scores pass validation, and unmatched player rows silently vanish from history
findings.acceptance: All result entry points reject impossible counters, absent/foreign IDs and inconsistent supported game structures.

findings.title: P1: dispute resolution can finalize a tied or internally contradictory official game
findings.acceptance: Correction accepts a fully validated revision; scores, innings, box and official projections reconcile atomically.

findings.title: P1: report approval, editing, and dispute are separate unversioned writes
findings.acceptance: Edit/confirm/dispute races, duplicate requests and interrupted commits accept exactly one revision.

findings.title: P1: save-state rollback is not a complete recovery mechanism
findings.acceptance: Mature-state restore preserves all intended tables, FK relationships, evidence and finalization identity.

findings.title: P1: snapshots can contain states that never existed together
findings.acceptance: Concurrent snapshots are wholly before or after a transaction; restore coordinates every relevant writer.

findings.title: P1: advance swallows failed finalizations, marks the stage done, and moves on
findings.acceptance: Failure of a required game prevents clock advancement; retry finishes missing work once without false news.

findings.title: P1: batched coach XP is lost on crashes, and postseason XP can miss the flush
findings.acceptance: Game and postseason coach records/XP survive crashes and replay with exactly-once durable effects.

findings.title: P1 for competitive record keeping: finalized evidence remains deletable and re-extractable
findings.acceptance: Approved evidence manifests and OCR revisions cannot be silently replaced/deleted; amendments remain auditable.

findings.title: P1 release-evidence gap: the 14-human launch test does not prove the handoff's promised workflow
findings.acceptance: Executable 14-coach end-to-end rehearsal proves promised workflow and fails certification on missing prerequisites.

findings.title: P2: the migration/release story needs a reproducible bootstrap and recovery contract
findings.acceptance: Empty bootstrap, upgrade, concurrent/interrupted migration and backup restore pass with readiness correctly gated.
findings.notes: W01 bootstrap slice verified: valid0032SQL, whole-file transactions, fresh20migrations, repeat/data preservation, orphan rollback/retry, HTTP readiness and independent QA. Full TI-12 remains open for W04 immutable baseline, historical upgrades, concurrency/checksums, awaited startup transformations and recovery. Batch 04 verifies actual entry-point startup on an empty bootstrapped fixture and preserves guest saves; asynchronous backfills, historical upgrades and recovery remain unverified.

findings.title: P2 reproducibility blocker: committed package URLs depend on Replit's private network
findings.acceptance: Clean locked install succeeds outside Replit with intended versions/integrity and documented runtimes.

findings.title: P1 under lease-loss conditions: a stale advancing worker is detected after it has already written
findings.acceptance: Expired/resumed worker cannot commit stale writes after a new lease owner begins.

findings.title: P1: Generated box scores are not accounts of the game [probed]
findings.acceptance: One event ledger reconciles score, runs, outs and opposing batting/pitching stats across fixtures and seeded campaign.

findings.title: P1: Full-season schedule bypasses the rotation/rest model [probed + proven]
findings.acceptance: Full catalog uses explicit ordered day slots and feasible byes; rest is committed before next team game.

findings.title: P1: Quick-sim lineup decisions barely exist in the result model [proven]
findings.acceptance: Only active participants drive game events; unequal active/bench and batting-order fixtures prove intended causality.

findings.title: P1: Starter selection and fatigue use different realities [probed + proven]
findings.acceptance: Selected scoring/event/box/rest pitcher agrees; fatigue and canonical pitcher positions affect legal staff use.

findings.title: P1: Power-ball is a dominant quick-sim strategy [proven; dominance is design analysis]
findings.acceptance: Strategy changes contextual risk/reward; benchmark different personnel to reject an unconditional dominant preset.

findings.title: P1: Promise fulfillment is random, including championships [proven]
findings.acceptance: Promise fulfillment uses authoritative achievements, opportunities and deadlines; missing evidence remains pending.

findings.title: P1: Pitcher wins/losses do not mean pitcher of record [proven]
findings.acceptance: Pitcher responsibility and external verified W/L/SV preserve correct decisions; unknown decisions are not guessed.

findings.title: P1: Play-by-play is a second incompatible simulator, not presentation [proven]
findings.acceptance: Quick and PBP/replay share the engine and produce equivalent official outcomes and statistics from identical inputs.

findings.title: P1: PBP has baseball state/scoring errors [proven from branches; not live-tested]
findings.acceptance: PBP baseball-state edge fixtures pass and event/box persistence preserves supported statistics.

findings.title: P1: Awards and legacy reward ratings, not the season [proven]
findings.acceptance: Qualified factual performance determines awards and correctly classified career achievements.

findings.title: P2: National selection incentivizes record accumulation without opponent quality [proven model; design judgment]
findings.acceptance: Chosen postseason preset, strength-of-schedule treatment and tiebreaks are transparent, reproducible and tested.

findings.title: P2: Recruiting AI's high-potential strategy is partially dead [proven]
findings.acceptance: CPU high-potential strategy handles numeric grades and respects scouting knowledge, needs and affordability.

findings.title: P2: Recruiting design rewards clicking the best multiplier and protecting sunk cost [design judgment grounded in code]
findings.acceptance: Same-cost policy experiments and fair tie resolution support multiple choices without alphabetical advantage.

findings.title: P2: Development has good structure but insufficient coaching agency [proven inputs + design judgment]
findings.acceptance: Bounded development choices create explainable differences and approved old/new Power Pros roster deltas.

findings.title: P2: Rich-get-richer economy needs proof of sustainable competition [proven multipliers; balance hypothesis]
findings.acceptance: 10-20-season campaigns evaluate parity, inflation and rebuild mobility; decision and any calibration pass retest.

findings.title: P1: Advanced stats are more confident than their data [proven]
findings.dependsOn: W06 provenance UI; W07 event stats
findings.acceptance: Counting stats and supported formulas are correct; inputs, units and coverage distinguish observed/derived/estimated/unknown.

findings.title: P1: The report form breaks its own promise about required work
findings.acceptance: Reporting requirements match policy and validators before entry begins, with linked field-level failures.

findings.title: P1: Manual reporting work can disappear without even the OCR warning
findings.acceptance: Manual/OCR drafts recover from refresh/interruption and expose offline, unsynced and conflicting edits.

findings.title: P1: Everyday feedback blocks the entire game, then vanishes too quickly
findings.acceptance: Routine feedback is nonblocking and accessible; errors persist with retained inputs and useful retry.

findings.title: P1: The hub has too many competing definitions of “what to do next”
findings.acceptance: Role/mode-specific Today exposes one next action without duplicate obligations at phone widths and zoom.

findings.title: P1: Navigation includes a destination that does not resolve to its promised content
findings.dependsOn: Early isolated fix allowed; W12 shell
findings.acceptance: Every navigation destination resolves correctly; News, refresh, Back and selected state have route assertions.

findings.title: P1: The keyboard and touch experience is inconsistent in core management controls
findings.acceptance: Keyboard and touch can inspect, assign and reorder the full roster; narrow widths/focus/zoom pass.

findings.title: P1: Statistics are presented with more certainty than the companion UI can justify
findings.acceptance: Reported unknown data never appears measured or as observed zero; provenance and coverage flow through UI/API.

findings.title: P2: The companion is a collection of screens rather than one game workspace
findings.acceptance: One stable game workspace shows exact roster/rules revision, evidence, state and permitted next action.

findings.title: P2: Creation starts with configuration scale instead of player intent
findings.acceptance: Solo/run/join intent selects reviewed presets; unfamiliar users reach their first meaningful task without admin confusion.

findings.title: P2: Narrative has personalities and consequences, but many choices read like answer-key tests
findings.acceptance: Reviewed dilemmas have defensible alternatives and ownership/costs; confirmed-game claims are evidence-linked.

findings.title: P2: History should explain why these players mattered
findings.acceptance: Unified player identity/history survives transfers, departures, corrections and archive navigation.

findings.title: P1: Correcting an OCR batter's displayed name does not repair its roster identity
findings.acceptance: Selecting the correct OCR batter changes roster ID while retaining extracted stats; submission then validates.
